messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,

I'm new to NicheMapR. I was thinking of modeling the potential distribution of the pasture mealybug (Heliococcus summervillei) using NicheMapR or modeling/analyzing the climatic suitability and identify seasonal activity patterns in a single location where mealybug has been recorded before, or a far-away independent location where it is not recorded and examining the feasibility of its survival over there.

The study on climatic requirements, biology, and other physiological parameters has not been done before. So, I was wondering if I could use Microclimate, or the Ectotherm model, either separately or together, to develop a model/do an analysis without having lab and field data. Also, if there is any other better way/ideas/function using which I could develop a distribution pattern, or identify how the mealybug interacts at a given location, climate.

Thank you.

regards,
Parbati Ghising

messages.body_plain:
Hi Parbati,
Welcome to the group. You really do need some data on the species to do something useful with NicheMapR. The value of a 'mechanistic niche modelling' approach to understanding species' environmental limits is that you can link what you know about the organism's traits. For example, you can compute how its rates (growth, development, movement, reproduction) respond to its body temperature, or how fast it looses water given its cuticle's resistance, etc. because the package allows you to incorporate its microclimatic conditions and behaviour to determine the environments it experiences and how that translates into body temperature and evaporation. Best thing is to look at published studies using the package to get a sense of what's involved. It takes a while to learn the background ideas behind the models to be able to apply them usefully.
Hope that helps,
All the best,
Mike

Hi everyone,
i am encountering a similar error. I donwnloaded the monthly era5 data, merged them using Kris's function and the regular micro_era5 runs are sensible (validated on some weather station data) although i do keep getting some rainfall warnings. They also give good predictions with ectotherm (deb=1).
Now, when i try to run the scenario = 2 or 4 things get out of hand, both TREF and TALOC are way too high, im talking about 70 degrees in the summer (values are almost double of what one would expect). Please find attached the regular scenario=0 test runs with observed temp data i used to validate the micro_era5.

If anyone has any advice im very much open to suggestions. I think i still might have some issues with compatibility between the emrged era5 data and the terracliamte scenarios data.

Here is my code to generate the micro objects in a loop, due to issues with snowfall and model crashing at low ERR values im permiting quite a high ERR but most locations work with the default value.

Cheers

Urban

getwd()

# Loop over each location
for (i in 1:nrow(locations_df)) {
  ERR <- 1.5
  # Extract location details
  name <- locations_df$Location[i]
  lat <- locations_df$Latitude[i]
  lon <- locations_df$Longitude[i]

  # Define the save path for the location
  save_path <- file.path(base_path, name)

  # Create the directory if it doesn't exist
  if (!dir.exists(save_path)) {
    dir.create(save_path, recursive = TRUE)
  }

  # Change working directory to the new folder
  setwd(save_path)

  # Get DEM data
  dem <- microclima::get_dem(r = NA, lat = lat, lon = lon, resolution = 30, zmin = -20, xdims = 100, ydims = 100)

  # Convert coordinates to a SpatVector and transform to match DEM CRS
  xy <- terra::vect(data.frame(x = lon, y = lat), geom = c("x", "y"), crs = "EPSG:4326")
  xy <- terra::project(xy, terra::crs(dem))

  # Extract elevation using the same method as slope
  elev <- terra::extract(dem, xy, method = "simple")[,2]

  # Compute slope and extract value at the location
  slope <- terra::extract(terra::terrain(dem, v = "slope", unit = "degrees"), xy)[,2]

  # Run micro_era5

    SLE = SLE,
    warm = warm,
    soilgrids = 0,

    dstart = dstart,
    dfinish = dfinish,

    Usrhyt = Usrhyt,

    dem = dem,

    ERR = ERR,
    save = 1,
    spatial = '../../../Micro_era5/Urban_downloads_era5/ERA5_yearly/ERA5',

    ERR <- ERR + 0.5
    micro <- micro_era5(
      SLE = SLE,
      warm = warm,
      soilgrids = 0,

      dstart = dstart,
      dfinish = dfinish,

      Usrhyt = Usrhyt,

      loc = c(lon, lat),

      snowmodel = 1,
      BulkDensity = BulkDensity,
      cap = cap,
      runmoist = 1,
      scenario = scenario,
      Density = Density,
      Thcond = Thcond,
      SpecHeat = SpecHeat,
      slope = slope,
      aspect = aspect,
      hori = hori,
      dem = dem,
      windfac = windfac,
      ERR = ERR,
      save = 2,
      spatial = '../../../Micro_era5/Urban_downloads_era5/ERA5_yearly/ERA5',
      cad.effects = FALSE
    )
    gc()
  }
  setwd(base_path)

  }

for (i in 1:nrow(locations_df)) {

  name <- locations_df$Location[i]
  lat <- locations_df$Latitude[i]
  lon <- locations_df$Longitude[i]

  # Define the save path for the location
  save_path <- file.path(base_path, name)

  # Create the directory if it doesn't exist
  if (!dir.exists(save_path)) {
    dir.create(save_path, recursive = TRUE)
  }

  # Change working directory to the new folder
  setwd(save_path)

  # Get DEM data
  dem <- microclima::get_dem(r = NA, lat = lat, lon = lon, resolution = 30, zmin = -20, xdims = 100, ydims = 100)

  # Convert coordinates to a SpatVector and transform to match DEM CRS
  xy <- terra::vect(data.frame(x = lon, y = lat), geom = c("x", "y"), crs = "EPSG:4326")
  xy <- terra::project(xy, terra::crs(dem))

  # Extract elevation using the same method as slope
  elev <- terra::extract(dem, xy, method = "simple")[,2]

  # Compute slope and extract value at the location
  slope <- terra::extract(terra::terrain(dem, v = "slope", unit = "degrees"), xy)[,2]

  # Compute aspect and extract value at the location
  aspect <- terra::extract(terra::terrain(dem, v = "aspect", unit = "degrees"), xy)[,2]

  # Compute horizon angles
  ha36 <- numeric(36)
  for (j in 0:35) {
    har <- microclima::horizonangle(dem, j * 10, terra::res(dem)[1])
    ha36[j + 1] <- atan(terra::extract(har, xy)[,2]) * (180/pi)
  }

    windfac = windfac,
    ERR = ERR,
    save = 1,
    spatial = '../../../Micro_era5/Urban_downloads_era5/ERA5_yearly/ERA5',
    cad.effects = FALSE
  )

    cat("model crashed, trying a higher error tolerance \n")
    ERR <- ERR + 0.5
    micro <- micro_era5(
      SLE = SLE,
      warm = warm,
      soilgrids = 0,

      dstart = dstart,
      dfinish = dfinish,

      Usrhyt = Usrhyt,
      DEP = DEP,
      REFL = REFL,
      minshade = minshade,

      loc = c(lon, lat),
      runshade = 1,
      run.gads = 1,
      snowmodel = 1,
      BulkDensity = BulkDensity,
      cap = cap,
      runmoist = 1,
      scenario = scenario,
      Density = Density,
      Thcond = Thcond,
      SpecHeat = SpecHeat,
      slope = slope,
      aspect = aspect,
      hori = hori,
      dem = dem,
      windfac = windfac,
      ERR = ERR,
      save = 2,
      spatial = '../../../Micro_era5/Urban_downloads_era5/ERA5_yearly/ERA5',

  ERR <- 1.5

Hello,

Background:
I am modeling the microclimate of a grasshopper in meadow sites along an elevational gradient in Colorado. Ultimately, I am and trying to find a range of different body temperatures (Tbs) the hopper could thermoregulate to. (As far as thermoregulation, I am doing my own rather coarse thing by letting them move towards their preferred body temperature with no energetic cost. I am not using any of the biophysical modeling capabilities of NicheMapR -- just microclimate.)

My workflow is era5 data -> micro_era5 microclimate data at different combinations of height and shading -> Tb (using the TrenchR package)

Question:
My issue right now is that I think I am getting too wide of a range of microclimates, particularly air temperatures (varying as a result of shading) and I don't know how to address it.

I'll talk a little bit more about my approach now. I represent 5 different possible microclimates based on a combination of height above the ground and degree of shading: four combinations of what I consider the "extremes" -- 1) 0.005m above the ground (so, on the soil) and no shading, 2) 0.005m above the ground and 90% shading, 3) 0.15m above the ground and no shading, 5) 0.15m above the ground and 90% shading -- and a more intermediate position 5) 0.03m above the ground and 30% shading (this one is excluded from the figure in my reprex just to keep things simple, but the data is there).

[Side note: For thermoregulation, I will calculate the Tb at each of these 5 microclimates and let the maximum and minimum Tb at each hour define the range of possible Tbs. Then the hopper can move as close as the range allows to their preferred body temperature of ~35C (so if the range includes 35C, their Tb is 35C.)]

I am getting a wider range of air temperatures than I would have expected (~10C in the sunniest part of the day) and I imagine the range of available Tbs will be quite broad in the middle of the day. Did I implement something wrong? Or was 90% shading too aggressive of an option (I was imagining a hopper still in a meadow -- not a forest -- but seeking shade under some vegetation)? (I can also see how 0.005m above the ground is going to be rather driven by soil temperature, but I am trying to represent grasshoppers that are on the ground.)

Reprex:
I've attached an image and a zipfile with a simplified reprex. Here is some more info regarding that:
1. Rplot.png: a little info in addition to what's in the legend... the brown lines represent soil surface temperatures (at different levels of shading), while the other lines represent air temperatures (at different heights above the ground and at different levels of shading)
2. The zipfile contains 3 .R files that are run in the following order (also contains their outputs, already generated for you... you may want to start by running the 3rd file to check reproduce the figure and look at the dataframe)
a) ERA5Downloader.R uses mcera5 to get the ERA data as .nc files
b) get_microclim.R uses micro_era5() to get the 5 microclimates I described above
c) viz_microclim() creates the attached plot

Thank you so much!

OK that worked - so, now I'll try and reply:

First thanks for the excellent detail in your question, and sounds like an interesting study.

When you simulate shade with the microclimate model it is as if you have an infinite plane of shading at that level altering the ground temperature and air temperature profiles. This would be representative of what conditions would be like in e.g. a very large bush or under a canopy. However, in your case of a meadow, because of the small area of shade and the fact that air is mixing, the air temperature would be pretty much the same in and out of the shade. So what I would do is simulate your grasshoppers under the same convective regime (air temp and wind speed) but just cut the solar down by the shade fraction. Depending on how much shade, you could change the long-wave radiation environment from open sky and sunlit ground to be equal to air temperature to account for the fact that the veg is probably roughly air temperature radiating down on the grasshopper (depends how much of the sky the grasshopper 'sees') and the surface of the ground may be cooler than the open ground due to the shade.

You might want to try the micro_usa function in addition to the micro_era5 function, which is based on the USA gridMET dataset and is extracted directly from the web via opendap, so no need to pre-download all the data like with ERA5 (it's daily rather than hourly but higher resolution). Also to save microclimate runs, you can just simulate at one height and then use the get_profile function (see here <https://groups.google.com/u/1/g/nichemapr/c/6ljJU89ReZk/m/FAg_aaVZAgAJ>) to get any other heights you like.

All the best,
Mike

Hi Mike,

Today I've been trying to install NicheMapR in a machine that runs archlinux, and that uses gfortran version 15.1.1. Installing it in Debian works fine, but it uses gfortran 12.2.0. With gfortran 15, when compiling the package i got:

Error: Interface mismatch in dummy procedure at (1) conflicts with (2): 'funwing' is not a function

I tried different things, but I only managed to compile the program passing a flag to the compiler forcing it to be less strict with interface mistmatches (and in general, as far as I undesrtand what the flag does). PKG_FFLAGS = -std=legacy

With that, the error turned into a warning and NicheMapR compiled. I don't think that this would cause any issue to users using an older version of gfortran (or in other OSs, I haven't tried any of those cases though), so it might be good to have that file in case gfortran is updated in other OSs.

All the best,
Urtzi

Hi David,

Good question. You can choose the orientation of the cylinder to the sun but the physical geometry is horizontal. The relevant code is below. You can make your own geometry function to accommodate your specific requirements. We will make a Julia version of this program in the near future which will make this kind of customisation much easier. There's no generic code for multi-part organisms at present in NicheMapR though I have recently made a human model which is present in the latest github version that is multi-part. It's a bit tricky, e.g. you need to account for the joins so there isn't too much surface area. I have a plan to include a generic multipart framework in the future but not sure when that will happen. Perhaps it is something that interested members of the group could collaborate on. Ofir Levy and his group are interested in this, for example.

All the best,
Mike

C     CYLINDER
      IF (INT(SHAPE) .EQ. 1) THEN
       R1 = (VOL/(SHAPEB*PI*2.))**(1./3.) !R_SKIN
       R2 = R1 + ZFUR ! R_FA
       ALENTH=SHAPEB*R1*2.
C      FUR-AIR AREA = END CIRCLE AREA + CIRCLE PERIMETER * LENGTH (LENGTH = 2*D2)
       AREASKIN=2.*PI*R1**2.+2.*PI*R1*ALENTH
       ATOT=2.*PI*R2**2.+2.*PI*R2*ALENTH
       AWIDTH=2.*R1
       AHEIT=AWIDTH
       AREA=ATOT
       IF((INT(SUBQFAT).EQ.1).AND.(MASFAT.GT.0.00))THEN
C       COMPUTE SUBQ FAT THICKNESS
        FLSHVL = VOL- VOLFAT
        RFLESH = SQRT(FLSHVL/(PI*ALENTH))
        FATTHK = R1 - RFLESH
       ELSE
        FLSHVL = VOL
        RFLESH = R1
        FATTHK = 0.
       ENDIF
       ASILN = AWIDTH * ALENTH
       ASILP = PI * R2**2.
       IF(INT(ORIENT).EQ.0)THEN ! AVERAGE POSTURE
        ASIL = (ASILN + ASILP)/2.
       ENDIF
       IF(INT(ORIENT).EQ.1)THEN ! NORMAL TO SUN'S RAYS (HEAT MAXIMISING)
        ASIL = ASILN
       ENDIF
       IF(INT(ORIENT).EQ.2)THEN ! PARALLEL TO SUN'S RAYS (HEAT MINIMISING)
        ASIL = ASILP
       ENDIF
       IF(INT(ORIENT).EQ.3)THEN
        ASIL=2.*R2*ALENTH*sin(ZEN*pi/180.)+pi*R2**2.*cos(ZEN*pi/180.)
       ENDIF
        D = VOL**(1./3.)
       GO TO 999
      ENDIF
